newsitem.title: USA: Aid to Bosnia not been enough - World Bank chief.
newsitem.headline: Aid to Bosnia not been enough - World Bank chief.

text.p: World Bank President James Wolfensohn told global economic policymakers on Thursday that financial help for war-torn Bosnia has fallen short of what was needed and urged them to do more.
"We have achieved a lot," Wolfensohn said. "But we should be realistic and straight-forward with each other. The pace of spending in Bosnia and Herzegovina has not been enough."
Donors have pledged $1.8 billion in financial help for Bosnia this year.

But only $558 million of that has been disbursed so far, according to a report released this week by the Bank and European Commission. Another $500 million or so is expected to be handed over to Bosnia by the end of the year.

In his closing speech to the annual International Monetary Fund/World Bank meeting, Wolfensohn said that donors need to spell out "precisely" what they plan to do and how they will work together when they gather at an aid conference for Bosnia early next year.
Bosnian Prime Minister Hasan Muratovic told the annual meeting on Tuesday that the world needed to do more to help his country.

"The reconstruction programme is the only hope for our country," Muratovic said. "Unfortunately, although this assistance is certainly remarkable from the donor standpoint, it has nonetheless proved insufficient to bring about significant progress so far," he added.
Muratovic has praised both the World Bank and the United States for delivering the money that has been promised. But he has been critical of Europe.
